sub_theme: Hydrogen production routes and costs (electrolysis, biomass gasification)
settings: multi-sector 1, power-generation-SIN 1, agriculture 1; La Guajira 1, Antioquia 1, no department 1
technical: LCOH most sensitive to electrolyzer investment cost and utilization rate [R0043]; capacity factor most influential parameter on LCOH [R0108]; technical-energy potential 2,084 TJ/yr, 91% pigs [R0314]
economic: Colombia LCOH solar PV $8.3-10.7/kg (2020) and $4.1-4.9/kg (2030) [R0043]; onshore wind $5.2-41.3/kg (2020) and $3.0-17.7/kg (2030) [R0043]; LCOH 7 USD/kg onshore wind AWE to 9.69 USD/kg offshore wind PEMWE [R0108]
pattern: R0043 and R0108 agree that utilisation or capacity factor drives hydrogen cost (R0043 also names electrolyzer investment cost), but report LCOH on different bases (solar PV $8.3-10.7/kg (2020) and $4.1-4.9/kg (2030), onshore wind $5.2-41.3/kg (2020) and $3.0-17.7/kg (2030) in R0043; 7 USD/kg onshore wind AWE to 9.69 USD/kg offshore wind PEMWE in R0108). R0314 is a biomass resource assessment (technical-energy potential 2,084 TJ/yr, 91% pigs), and none of the three quantifies environmental outcomes.

sub_theme: Hydrogen life-cycle emissions, blue hydrogen, CO2 capture and storage, and CO2/methanol valorisation
methods: modelling/simulation 3 (R0160, R0350, R0369); techno-economic assessment 2 (R0256, R0315); other 1 (R0203)
settings: industry 3, multi-sector 3; Santander 3, La Guajira 2, Bolívar 1, no department 1
technical: Guajira Basin most suitable, storage resources 3.2 Gt [R0315]; 2030 demand needs about 1.3 GW solar and 2.6 GW wind [R0203]; methanol yield +5% (2.42 to 2.54 kg MeOH/kg gas) [R0160]; methanol output +5% [R0256]; energy consumption -30 to 53% [R0160]; refinery needs 5-6x renewable electricity [R0369]
economic: transport and storage costs 3.2-48 EUR/tCO2 [R0315]; LCOM 456-492 USD/ton vs 612-645 base [R0256]; green methanol LCOM 659-737 USD/ton [R0256]; viable up to CO2 price 140 EUR/t (medium) and 205 EUR/t (high complexity) [R0369]; net margin high complexity -40% short, -5% long term [R0369]
environmental: SMR 10.33, SMR+CCS 1.96, wind electrolysis 0.84, hydro 1.51, PV 3.88, grid electrolysis 11.32 kg CO2-eq/kg H2 [R0203]; wind electrolysis ~6 t CO2/t LH2 vs coal electrolysis 66 t CO2/t LH2 [R0350]; CCS cuts gasification CO2 from 31 to 11 t but raises VOC 37% [R0350]; CO2 vent -62% [R0160, R0256]; global warming -50% [R0160]
pattern: R0160 and R0256 independently report the same +5% methanol output and -62% CO2 vent for the heat-pump/SMR-based design with cost gains (LCOM 456-492 USD/ton vs 612-645 base in R0256), while R0369 shows that refinery hydrogen profitability hinges on CO2 price (viable up to 140 EUR/t at medium complexity). R0203 and R0350 agree that wind-powered electrolysis has the lowest emissions and grid or coal pathways the highest (functional units differ), CCS lowers CO2 at a cost in other impacts (R0350), and R0315 identifies the Guajira Basin as most suitable for storage (3.2 Gt).

sub_theme: Hydrogen applications and roadmaps, and small modular nuclear reactors
methods: techno-economic assessment 1 (R0024); empirical case study 1 (R0148); modelling/simulation 1 (R0240); literature review 1 (R0381)
settings: power-generation-SIN 2, non-interconnected-zones 1, multi-sector 1; La Guajira 2, no department 2
technical: diesel use 87% lower than base case [R0024]; batteries needed when FC life near 15,000 h [R0024]; hybrid needed grid backup only a few days in Nov 2022 and Feb-Mar 2023 [R0148]; ~10 operating green H2 projects, 0.36 MW electrolysis [R0381]; 1-3 GW electrolysis target [R0381]; coal emission factor correlation 0.86 and SMR capacity factor 0.51 [R0240]
economic: LCOE about 0.112 USD/kWh, NPC 6.03 M USD [R0024]; green LCOH USD 1.7/kg and 50 kt blue H2 at USD 2.4/kg 2030 targets [R0381]; projected cost falls to 1.59 USD/kg in La Guajira by 2050 [R0381]
environmental: avoided emissions 82.62 MtCO2eq (deterministic) vs Monte Carlo median 76.04 MtCO2eq [R0240]
pattern: R0024 (HOMER) and R0148 (empirical case) show that fuel-cell hybrids reduce diesel use or grid backup in off-grid settings (diesel use 87% lower in R0024), though their metrics are not directly comparable. R0381 shows a large gap between 2030 targets (green LCOH USD 1.7/kg, 1-3 GW electrolysis) and current deployment (~10 operating green H2 projects, 0.36 MW electrolysis), and R0240 reports that the SMR avoided-emission estimate is similar under deterministic and Monte Carlo treatment (82.62 vs 76.04 MtCO2eq). Each of these four uses rests on a single study.
